components.name: Grooved Coupling — Flexible
components.description: Two-segment mechanical coupling with controlled clearance between the housing key and the groove, permitting limited angular deflection, expansion and contraction at each joint. Used where movement, misalignment or vibration must be absorbed.
components.ratingNote: AWWA C606 standardises the groove and shoulder geometry, not ASME pressure classes. The working pressure of the coupling is declared by the manufacturer for each diameter and verified by hydrostatic test; the purchaser must specify the required internal working pressure.

standards.note: Groove geometry on the pipe end. Coupling pressure rating is manufacturer-specific.

fabricationNotes: Groove dimensions depend on pipe size, wall thickness and groove method. Take them from AWWA C606 or the coupling manufacturer, never by measurement of an existing joint.
Roll grooving cold-forms the groove and does not remove material. Cut grooving removes wall material and imposes a minimum wall thickness limit.
Roll-grooved and cut-grooved ends are not interchangeable.
Pipe ends must be square, clean and free of burrs, weld spatter and coating inside the gasket seat area.
Gasket compound must be selected for the service fluid and temperature. It is the sealing element, not the housing.
Allowable deflection per joint is limited and size-dependent. Take the value from the manufacturer; do not assume it.
Cumulative deflection across several joints is often used for gradual direction changes, within the per-joint limit.

referenceCompatibility.note: The grooved-end interface is defined by AWWA C606, not by any single manufacturer. Brands are named for identification purposes only, to state that this generic record describes the same standardised joint type those systems are built around. No manufacturer data is reproduced and no product-to-product interchangeability is asserted: always confirm groove profile, preparation method, allowable deflection and working pressure against the coupling manufacturer's own documentation.

components.name: Grooved Coupling — Rigid
components.description: Two-segment mechanical coupling that clamps into grooved pipe ends to form a rigid joint. The housing engages both grooves to restrain angular and axial movement, producing a joint that behaves closer to a flanged connection than to a flexible one.
components.ratingNote: AWWA C606 standardises the groove and shoulder geometry, not ASME pressure classes. The working pressure of the coupling is declared by the manufacturer for each diameter and verified by hydrostatic test; the purchaser must specify the required internal working pressure.

standards.note: Groove geometry on the pipe end. Coupling pressure rating is manufacturer-specific.

fabricationNotes: Groove dimensions depend on pipe size, wall thickness and groove method. Take them from AWWA C606 or the coupling manufacturer, never by measurement of an existing joint.
Roll grooving cold-forms the groove and does not remove material. Cut grooving removes wall material and imposes a minimum wall thickness limit.
Roll-grooved and cut-grooved ends are not interchangeable.
Pipe ends must be square, clean and free of burrs, weld spatter and coating inside the gasket seat area.
Gasket compound must be selected for the service fluid and temperature. It is the sealing element, not the housing.
Rigid couplings restrain movement: the system must accommodate thermal expansion elsewhere.

referenceCompatibility.note: The grooved-end interface is defined by AWWA C606, not by any single manufacturer. Brands are named for identification purposes only, to state that this generic record describes the same standardised joint type those systems are built around. No manufacturer data is reproduced and no product-to-product interchangeability is asserted: always confirm groove profile, preparation method and working pressure against the coupling manufacturer's own documentation.

PB-STD-API-594.title: Check Valves: Flanged, Lug, Wafer, and Butt-Welding
PB-STD-API-594.scope: This standard covers design, materials, face-to-face dimensions, pressure-temperature ratings, examination, inspection, and testing requirements for check valves with flanged, lug, wafer, and butt-welding ends.

PB-STD-API-600.title: Steel Gate Valves — Flanged, Threaded, and Welding Ends, Bolted Bonnets
PB-STD-API-600.scope: This standard covers requirements for bolted-bonnet, gate valves with flanged, butt-welding, and threaded ends in sizes NPS 1/2 through NPS 24, in pressure classes 150, 300, 600, 900, 1500, and 2500.

PB-STD-API-602.title: Steel Gate, Globe, and Check Valves for Sizes DN 100 (NPS 4) and Smaller
PB-STD-API-602.scope: This standard covers compact steel gate, globe, and check valves for petroleum and natural gas industries in sizes DN 100 (NPS 4) and smaller, covering flanged, threaded, welding, and flared ends.

PB-STD-API-608.title: Metal Ball Valves — Flanged, Threaded, and Welding Ends
PB-STD-API-608.scope: This standard covers requirements for soft-seated and metal-seated ball valves with flanged, butt-welding, and threaded ends for general petroleum and industrial applications.

PB-STD-ASME-B1-20-1.title: Pipe Threads, General Purpose (Inch)
PB-STD-ASME-B1-20-1.scope: This Standard covers dimensions and gaging for the most common inch pipe threads used for pressure-tight joints on pipe and fittings: NPT (National Pipe Taper), NPSC (National Pipe Straight Coupling), NPTR (National Pipe Taper Railing), NPSM (National Pipe Straight Mechanical), and NPSL (National Pipe Straight Locknut).

PB-STD-ASME-B16-10.title: Face-to-Face and End-to-End Dimensions of Valves
PB-STD-ASME-B16-10.scope:
This Standard covers face-to-face and end-to-end dimensions of straightway
valves, and center-to-face and center-to-end dimensions of angle valves.
Its purpose is to ensure that valves made by different manufacturers are
interchangeable in a piping system with respect to laying length.

PB-STD-ASME-B16-11.title: Forged Fittings, Socket-Welding and Threaded
PB-STD-ASME-B16-11.scope: This Standard covers ratings, dimensions, tolerances, marking, and material requirements for socket-welding and threaded forged fittings in sizes NPS 1/8 through NPS 4.

PB-STD-ASME-B16-20.title: Metallic Gaskets for Pipe Flanges: Ring-Joint, Spiral-Wound, and Jacketed
PB-STD-ASME-B16-20.scope: This Standard covers materials, dimensions, tolerances, and markings for metallic gaskets known as ring-joint, spiral-wound, and jacketed, and metal-clad and grooved metal gaskets with or without fillers for use with ASME B16.5 and B16.47 flanges.

PB-STD-ASME-B16-25.title: Buttwelding Ends
PB-STD-ASME-B16-25.scope: This Standard covers preparation of weld ends for butt welding of pipe, flanges, fittings, valves, and other piping components. Includes dimensions and tolerances for butt weld end bevel preparation, alignment, and internal machining requirements for wall thicknesses covered by other governing dimensional standards (e.g., ASME B16.9, B16.11, B16.34, B36.10M, B36.19M).

PB-STD-ASME-B16-48.title: Line Blanks
PB-STD-ASME-B16-48.scope: This Standard covers pressure-temperature ratings, materials, dimensions, tolerances, marking, and testing for operating line blanks (paddle blanks or paddle spacers) and spectacle blinds in sizes NPS 1/2 through NPS 24 for installation between ASME B16.5 flanges.

PB-STD-ASME-B16-5.title: Pipe Flanges and Flanged Fittings: NPS 1/2 Through NPS 24 Metric/Inch Standard
PB-STD-ASME-B16-5.scope: This Standard covers pressure-temperature ratings, materials, dimensions, tolerances, marking, testing, and methods of designating openings for pipe flanges and flanged fittings in sizes NPS 1/2 through NPS 24, and in rating Classes 150, 300, 400, 600, 900, 1500, and 2500.

PB-STD-ASME-B16-9.title: Factory-Made Wrought Buttwelding Fittings
PB-STD-ASME-B16-9.scope:
This Standard covers overall dimensions, tolerances, ratings, testing,
and markings for wrought factory-made buttwelding fittings in sizes
NPS 1/2 through 48 (DN 15 through DN 1200).

PB-STD-ASME-B18-2-2.title: Nuts for General Applications: Machine Screw Nuts, and Hex, Square, Hex Flange, and Coupling Nuts (Inch Series)
PB-STD-ASME-B18-2-2.scope: This Standard covers general and dimensional data for inch series square and hex nuts, including machine screw nuts and coupling nuts. Includes appendices on gaging of slots in slotted nuts, wrench openings for nuts, and formulas on which dimensional data are based.

PB-STD-ASME-B36-10M.title: Welded and Seamless Wrought Steel Pipe
PB-STD-ASME-B36-10M.scope: Covers the standardization of dimensions of welded and seamless wrought steel pipe for high or low temperatures and pressures.

PB-STD-MANUFACTURER-GENERIC.title: Generic Manufacturer Standard (Placeholder)
PB-STD-MANUFACTURER-GENERIC.scope: Placeholder standard for components that follow general industry practice but are not covered by a specific normative standard. Used when no ASME/API/MSS standard directly applies.

PB-STD-MSS-SP97.title: Integrally Reinforced Forged Branch Outlet Fittings — Socket Welding, Threaded, and Buttwelding Ends
PB-STD-MSS-SP97.scope: This Standard Practice covers integrally reinforced forged branch outlet fittings with socket welding, threaded, and buttwelding ends for use in Class 3000 and Class 6000 pressure piping systems.

PB-STD-AWWA-C606.title: Grooved and Shouldered Joints
PB-STD-AWWA-C606.scope:
This Standard covers grooved and shouldered type joints for use in piping
systems, including the dimensions of the grooves and shoulders, and the
requirements for the couplings that engage them. It is the vendor-neutral
reference for grooved end preparation; individual coupling manufacturers
publish their own product dimensions and pressure ratings on top of it.
